position: Current Regulations That Should Be Rolled Back (Civil Rights Data Collection)
proposal: The Mandate recommends that the Department rescind the Biden-era changes to the Civil Rights Data Collection that added a nonbinary sex category and retired data on high school single-sex athletics sports, teams and participants. It also recommends issuing a new CRDC that collects data directly relevant to the Office for Civil Rights' statutory enforcement authority.

status_summary: ED submitted a revised Civil Rights Data Collection for the 2025-26 and 2027-28 school years to OMB, with a 30-day notice published 2025-08-07 (90 FR 38137; comments closed 2025-09-08) that describes refining, adding and removing data elements without listing them. OMB's reginfo.gov record shows the revision (OMB control number 1870-0504) approved with change on 2026-07-20, with an expiration of 2029-07-31. According to K-12 Dive on 2026-07-31, the approved collection drops the nonbinary category, so schools report students as male or female, and removes gender identity from the rape and sexual assault definitions, with ED citing costs outweighing benefits and Executive Order 14168; NPR reported on 2026-09-04 that the delayed 2023-24 data release omitted nonbinary information and that ED had begun collecting data for the next cycles. Whether the single-sex athletics items are in the approved collection was not confirmed, and no ED statement tying the collection to OCR's statutory enforcement authority was located; the stage rests on the reported removal of the nonbinary category, which the primary notice does not itself describe.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14168 was signed, setting a federal policy of recognizing two sexes, male and female; ED later cited it in explaining the CRDC changes, per K-12 Dive.

ED published a Paperwork Reduction Act 30-day notice submitting a revised CRDC (OMB control number 1870-0504, docket ED-2024-SCC-0128) for the 2025-26 and 2027-28 collections; comments closed 2025-09-08.
K-12 Dive reported that the proposal would stop collecting data on nonbinary and transgender students and remove gender identity from the rape definition, as aligned with the 2020 Title IX rule.
OMB concluded its review of the revised CRDC information collection as approved with change, with an expiration date of 2029-07-31.
timeline.source: Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs (reginfo.gov)

timeline.event: K-12 Dive reported that the approved 2025-26 collection drops the nonbinary category and gender identity wording in the rape and sexual assault definitions, and that districts that had recorded nonbinary students must recode them as male or female.

NPR reported that the 2023-24 CRDC data released by ED omitted information on nonbinary students, that the 2025-26 collection eliminates the nonbinary category, and that a department spokesperson confirmed data collection for the next cycles had begun.

title: Drop the CRDC nonbinary category, keep athletics data, refocus CRDC on OCR enforcement
uncertainties: The Federal Register notice of 2025-08-07 and the reginfo.gov ICR page were re-read in review; neither lists individual data elements or mentions the nonbinary category, gender identity or athletics, and the notice points to the supporting statement and attachments. The Supporting Statement Part A for the collection (OMB control number 1870-0504, dated June 2026 with no day) was read on reginfo.gov on 2026-10-26: at Item 1, Section D (pages 10 to 11) it states that OCR proposes the retirement of the nonbinary category and the gender identity category from the CRDC, quotes the retired definition of nonbinary, cites Executive Order 14168 and retires the gender identity harassment data item. The statement is the agency's proposal; OMB approved the collection with change on 2026-07-20, and the terms of that change (the notice of action or terms of clearance) were not found on a qualifying host, so that the approved collection omits the nonbinary category rests on the supporting statement together with K-12 Dive and NPR reporting. Other specific changes (rape and sexual assault definitions, LGBTQ harassment items) come from K-12 Dive and NPR reporting and from a multistate attorneys general comment letter on the proposal (oag.ca.gov); the comment response on reginfo.gov was not opened. The ED CRDC background page on ed.gov (no date printed), which returned an error earlier, was read on 2026-10-26; per the research pass it describes the withdrawal of the January 2025 ICR on 2025-02-10 and the replacement ICR posted in August 2025, though the passage quoted from it does not itself state those dates. No source read mentions athletics in the 2025-26 proposal or approval: the supporting statement, K-12 Dive, NPR and an EdSurge report of 2025-10-06 are silent on it. A vendor help page (kb.infinitecampus.com) shows single-sex athletics questions in the 2021-22 collection, which suggests the retirement the Mandate objected to may not have taken effect, but this was not confirmed from ED documents. The Mandate refers to the December 2021 notice for the 2021-22 collection. No ED statement tying the collection to OCR's statutory enforcement authority was located. A refutation check on 2026-10-24 found no court challenge to the 2025-26 collection and no later Federal Register notice; coverage in K-12 Dive of 2026-09-03 and AP reporting carried by Civil Beat of 2026-09-09 does not address single-sex athletics items.
